title: 35 Self Hosted Projects on GitHub: Usertour, Alexandrie, homelable, Frontman, nylon, TuneLog, midday

sections.title: Introduction
paragraphs: Welcome back to GitHub Awesome. Today we're looking at 35 self-hosted projects on GitHub. Let's get into it. User tour is a self-hostable alternative to app cues and user flow for building onboarding directly inside your product.

sections.title: Usertour
paragraphs: You can create guided tours, checklists, launchers, and surveys, then target them using custom user attributes and tracked events. It also keeps versions across staging and production with analytics for views, completions, and drop off points.

sections.title: Alexandrie
paragraphs: Alexandria is a self-hosted offline first knowledge base that sits between Notion, Obsidian, and Confluence. Its markdown editor handles diagrams, latex, snippets, and interactive elements, while the workspace model adds teams, nested documents, and granular access rules. Permissions run five levels deep per document per user and the PWA keeps working with no connection.

sections.title: homelable
paragraphs: Home label turns a messy Home Lab spreadsheet into an interactive network map with live status built in. It can scan your local network, Q discovered devices for approval and monitor each node through ping, HTTP, TCP or service health endpoints. Proxmox, ziggb, and z-wave imports fill the canvas automatically, while floor plans and custom layouts keep it readable.

sections.title: Frontman
paragraphs: Frontman is a coding agent that starts from the running browser, then works backward to the source file behind whatever you clicked. It reads the live DOM, computed CSS, component tree, and server logs. So, a request like fixing card spacing comes with context terminal agents usually miss. Changes land in the actual codebase with hot reload and a reviewable diff.

sections.title: nylon
paragraphs: Nylon is a self-healing wireguard mesh that keeps traffic moving when links fail without relying on a central coordination server. Nodes exchange routes directly and use measured latency to choose the best multihop path, so machines don't all need direct connectivity. The project targets recovery in under 10 seconds after a failure, while stock WireGuard clients can join through a gateway.

sections.title: TuneLog
paragraphs: Tounel log gives Navadrome a recommendation engine that learns from what you actually do instead of asking you to rate every song. Skips lower a track score, full plays raise it, and repeats count even more with recency and discovery mixed into the final playlists. It can also sync your library, improve search with fuzzy matching, and pull collaborative suggestions from listenrains.

sections.title: USBridge-Remote
paragraphs: USB bridge remote puts hardware KVM access and software remote desktop in one client, so the same dashboard can reach a machine before boot or after the operating system loads. The agent handles screen capture and remote input, while Tailscale provides encrypted peer-to-peer networking without manual port forwarding. It also supports moonlight-based streaming and clients across desktop and mobile platforms.

sections.title: rocketplaneIO
paragraphs: Rocketplane is a self-hosted AI S sur for Kubernetes that can investigate incidents and apply fixes without handing an LLM unrestricted cubectale access. EBPF tracing map service traffic without changing application code. Then the copilot proposes actions from a fixed risk graded catalog. Each change runs through approval, verification, and automatic roll back. if the cluster doesn't converge.

sections.title: compdf-self-hosted
paragraphs: Comp PDF self-hosted is a Docker deployed document processing platform for teams that don't want files leaving their infrastructure. It puts PDF editing, merging, splitting, encryption, and conversion behind both a browser interface and an API with support for Office files, images, HTML, and structured text formats. The admin console tracks API keys, usage, licenses, and operation logs.

sections.title: email-to-print
paragraphs: Email to print turns an ordinary mailbox into a private print queue without routing family documents through a printer vendor's cloud. A small Python service watches a dedicated folder, rejects senders outside your allow list, converts office attachments with Libra Office, and hands printable files to cups. It can even print the email body and send a confirmation afterward.

sections.title: midday
paragraphs: Midday brings invoicing, time tracking, receipt matching, and financial reporting into one workspace built for freelancers. If your business admin lives across disconnected tabs and subscriptions, this is the consolidation play. Magic Inbox pairs receipts with transactions, the tracker connects hours to projects, and Vault keeps contracts close to the numbers.

sections.title: PortalJS
paragraphs: Portal.js turns a data portal brief into plain editable Nex.js JS instead of trapping you inside a proprietary builder. Its agent skills can recommend an architecture, scaffold the home, catalog, and data set pages, then load CSV, JSON, or GOJSON. A single data provider contract lets the frontend move from static files to CCAN or open metadata without rewriting every page.

sections.title: tududi
paragraphs: To duty is a self-hosted life and project organizer that keeps tasks, notes, and planning data on your own server. The hierarchy is practical. Areas contain projects. Projects collect tasks and notes and tags cut across everything. Recurring tasks handle completionbased schedules, while Telegram gives you quick capture and daily digests.

sections.title: dashwise
paragraphs: Dashwise is a self-hosted home lab dashboard you configure through the interface. So adding services doesn't mean living in YAML. It keeps links, search, and notifications in one start page with widgets for things like weather and bessel. RSS subscriptions can turn the same screen into a compact news reader. Enough monitoring to be useful without pretending to replace your actual observability stack.

sections.title: kandev
paragraphs: Kanddev is a self-hosted control plane for running coding agents in parallel with review built into the workflow instead of bolted on afterward. Tasks live on a canbon board. Each agent gets an isolated git work tree and the workspace keeps code terminals, browser previews, and diffs together. It supports multiple agent providers and local docker or SSH execution.

sections.title: 4gaBoards
paragraphs: 4GA boards is a self-hosted Canbon app for teams that want realtime collaboration without handing project data to a SAS vendor. Its hierarchy runs from projects down to individual tasks, while collapsible lists keep larger boards readable. You can edit a card and rearrange the board at the same time without losing local description changes. Trello import is built in. Docker compose Postgres behind it.

sections.title: diction
paragraphs: Diction speech to text into a full iOS keyboard, so dictation works inside any app instead of living in a separate recorder. You can run Whisper or Parakeet directly on the phone, point it at any OpenAI compatible transcription server, or self-host the included encrypted gateway. The same keyboard can also compose and rewrite text through custom AI modes.

sections.title: Airpipe
paragraphs: Airpipe sends files between the terminal and a browser using a short passphrase without setting up SSH accounts or uploading everything to permanent storage. In direct mode, the devices pair through a relay and stream over WebRTC while the relay sees only cipher text. If both sides can't be online together, mailbox mode holds the encrypted file briefly. The same phrase works from CLI, browser, or QR code.

sections.title: shelftxt
paragraphs: Shelf text is a multi-user reading tracker that ranks your ownto- read shelf with transparent rules instead of a mystery recommendation feed. Each account gets separate book data in postgresql with statuses, progress, ratings, and CSV backup. The fast API endpoint scores unread books from author preferences in your reading history. And the logic lives in a clean isolated ranking layer. Uptime kit combines self-hosted uptime monitoring with public status pages. And its real differentiator is distributed probing.

sections.title: uptimekit
paragraphs: You can run multiple workers in different locations, checking HTTP or TCP services, while the central app handles assignments, incidents, and response time history. Teams and organizations are built in, and ClickHouse is optional for deeper analytics.

sections.title: Routario
paragraphs: Rutario is a self-hosted fleet platform that connects directly to GPS hardware, so vehicle locations and sensor data stay on infrastructure you control. It understands eight native tracker protocols, draws live positions on a map, and replays trips with sensor graphs. Alerts cover geoences, speeding, idling, and maintenance with routing to channels like email or Telegram.

sections.title: Rootprint
paragraphs: Rootprint is a self-hosted log platform that puts full text search over object storage instead of asking you to operate a stateful elastic search style cluster. It accepts logs through open telemetry, indexes them with quickwit, and keeps the underlying splits in S3 compatible storage. The UI stays focused on incident work, field filters, histograms, saved queries, and surrounding log context.

sections.title: moneat
paragraphs: Monot is a self-hosted observability stack designed to accept the tooling you already have, including Sentry SDKs, data dog agents, and open telemetry exporters. That means errors, traces, logs, metrics, replays, uptime checks, and feature flags can land in one system without rewriting every integration. Click house handles the heavy side while PostgresQL and Reddus support the rest.

sections.title: FreeFrame
paragraphs: Freeframe is a self-hosted media review workspace that keeps production files and client feedback on infrastructure you control. Reviewers can leave frame accurate comments, draw directly on video or images, and compare two revisions side by side with synchronized playback. The practical win comes after review. Comments export as timeline markers for Final Cut Pro or Premiere. KBORP makes another computer's files appear as a

sections.title: KeibiDrop
paragraphs: real folder on your machine, so you can open a large file before the transfer finishes. Its fuse mode lets native apps, editors, and even git work against the remote folder while changes sync back. It discovers peers automatically on a LAN, then chooses a direct path or an encrypted relay across the internet.

sections.title: grimoire
paragraphs: Grimmoire turns a folder full of tabletop RPG PDFs into a self-hosted campaign library. Instead of making you hunt through file names midsession, it indexes every page with SQLite full text search, uses OCR for scanned books, and serves a mobile friendly page viewer. Maps, tokens, audio, bookmarks, and campaign notes live beside the rule books while the source files stay mounted readonly.

sections.title: NotesMe
paragraphs: Notesme is a self-hosted notes app for people who want folders and version history without deploying a whole knowledge platform. The front end uses plain JavaScript with no framework or bundler, while fast API and SQLite keep the backend compact. You get nested folders, automatic snapshots, offline read access, and optional encryption for note content at rest.

sections.title: f360-vision
paragraphs: F3 vision puts industrial point clouds and panoramic imagery in one viewer, so factory scans are more than static files on a workstation. You can navigate the 3D scene in a browser, inspect measurements, and view panoramas for visual context. It runs as a desktop app or through a Dockerhosted server, including onremise deployments.

sections.title: Linse
paragraphs: Lince is a self-hosted event photo wall where guests scan a QR code and start sharing without creating accounts. They can upload, browse, tag, like, and comment. with new photos appearing live. The host gets moderation controls and can export the originals to a local folder. It also strips XIF metadata during upload, which is a thoughtful default when dozens of phones are feeding one private event gallery.

sections.title: jarvis
paragraphs: Jarvis is a self-hosted voice assistant where speech recognition, voice generation, and command routing can stay on your own hardware. It uses Whisper for transcription, Piper or Cocooro for speech, and can identify different household speakers for personal context. You can bring a cloud model or run one locally, then extend commands through packages.

sections.title: ignis
paragraphs: Ignis runs Obsidian as an actual self-hosted web app instead of streaming a desktop through VNC. It replaces the Electron APIs Obsidian expects with browser compatible versions while keeping Vault files on your server. Core editing, canvas, themes, and many community plugins work, plus live sync between tabs. Some node dependent plugins won't load, and Ignis has no built-in authentication, so don't expose it raw.

sections.title: Isola
paragraphs: Isola gives AI agents somewhere safer to run generated code, disposable sandboxes on your own Kubernetes cluster. Each pod uses G Visor for an extra application kernel boundary, starts with network access denied, and can enforce per sandbox resource limits. Its Python, TypeScript, and REST APIs handle commands, files, and streamed output.

sections.title: LAN-Orangutan
paragraphs: LAN orangutan turns basic network scans into a persistent inventory for your own home lab. It uses end mapap to discover devices, then lets you attach names, groups, and notes so the same mystery IP doesn't confuse you next week. The web dashboard tracks online status across multiple networks, while the CLI returns JSON for scripts. Tailscale support also brings remote nodes into the same view, which is handy once the lab escapes one subnet. Timelot is a self-hosted

sections.title: tymeslot
paragraphs: scheduling platform that keeps booking pages, calendar data, and meeting automation on infrastructure you control. It checks connected calendars at booking time to block conflicts, then can create a video room and send confirmation emails with calendar files. Availability rules cover buffers, holidays, and minimum notice.

sections.title: wardnet
paragraphs: Wardnet turns a Linux box or Raspberry Pi into a privacy gateway for every device on your network, including gadgets that can't run VPN software themselves. You can route devices through different WireGuard tunnels, apply separate DNS block lists, and isolate IoT or guest hardware with firewall zones. It also handles local DNS and DHCP from one dashboard.
